name: Oracle Cloud
tagline: Enterprise cloud VMs with a genuinely free-forever compute tier for small sites
description: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure offers pay-as-you-go Compute VM instances for hosting, plus an Always Free tier with real forever-free VM capacity.
about: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI) is a large enterprise cloud platform covering databases, AI, and enterprise applications — this listing covers only its Compute VM instances as a self-managed website-hosting option, not the wider Oracle enterprise catalog.

The notable part for small-site hosting is OCI's Always Free tier: it includes up to two VM.Standard.E2.1.Micro AMD instances (1/8 OCPU, 1 GB RAM each, 50 GB boot volume) plus Ampere A1 Arm compute — currently 1,500 OCPU-hours and 9,000 GB-hours per month (equivalent to 2 OCPUs / 12 GB RAM run continuously), down from the original 4 OCPU / 24 GB after Oracle quietly cut the allowance in mid-2026. Always Free also bundles 200 GB combined block storage, 10 TB/month outbound data transfer, and a flexible load balancer — enough to run a real low-traffic site or VPS-style server at $0.

Beyond the free tier, standard x86 Compute (VM.Standard.E4.Flex) is billed at $0.0255 per OCPU-hour plus $0.0015 per GB-memory-hour; Ampere A1 usage beyond the free allowance runs $0.01 per OCPU-hour plus $0.0015 per GB-hour. There's no managed cPanel-style hosting plan — you provision and administer the VM yourself, which puts this squarely in DIY/technical-user territory rather than beginner shared hosting.
policies: Oracle Cloud's Always Free resources genuinely don't expire or convert to a trial — they remain free for the life of the account as long as usage stays within the published limits; exceeding a limit (e.g. running more Ampere A1 OCPUs than the current 2-OCPU allowance) can result in the excess instance being reclaimed rather than silently billed.

New sign-ups also get $300 in free credits for 30 days to try paid services, separate from the permanent Always Free resources. Paid Compute usage is billed monthly in arrears based on actual OCPU/memory/storage consumption; there's no fixed-term contract or long-term-prepay discount structure like typical shared-hosting plans.
